---
title: "Rules and their sources"
---

Every phone-number rule in `dialtone` comes from Google's
[`libphonenumber`](https://github.com/google/libphonenumber) project, pinned to
release `v9.0.43`. This page lists what already existed on CRAN, what is bundled
and what is left out, how the XML numbering-plan metadata are compiled, and how
parity with the Python `phonenumbers` port is verified.

## Why this package

A column of phone numbers in survey or administrative data raises four routine
questions:

1. Is each value a well-formed phone number (`phone_valid()`) or at least a
   possible length (`phone_possible()`)?
2. Which country or non-geographic numbering plan does it belong to
   (`phone_region()`)?
3. What kind of line is it — fixed line, mobile, toll-free, VoIP, premium rate
   (`phone_type()`)?
4. What is its canonical E.164, international, national or RFC 3966 form
   (`phone_format()`)?

`dialtone` answers those questions for a character vector at once, without
requiring a Java installation, without making network requests at run time, and
returning `FALSE` or `NA` on malformed values rather than stopping.

It validates the *numbering plan* of a number. It cannot say whether a number
has been assigned to a subscriber or is currently active.

## What already exists

### On CRAN

| Package | License | Covers | Why it is not enough here |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`dialr`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=dialr) | GPL-3 | Wraps the Java `libphonenumber` `.jar` (`dialrjars`) via `rJava` | Requires a working Java runtime and `rJava`, which frequently breaks in headless, container or student environments; GPL-3. |
| [`idcheck`](https://github.com/gojiplus/idcheck) | MIT | National identity schemes and check digits, including `in_mobile` | `in_mobile` is a single ten-digit Indian format rule, not `libphonenumber`. |

### Elsewhere

| Project | License | Used how |
|---|---|---|
| [Google `libphonenumber`](https://github.com/google/libphonenumber) `v9.0.43` | Apache-2.0 | Upstream source of `data-raw/upstream/PhoneNumberMetadata.xml` (SHA-256 `5bbfb6f2e63ba1131fc867cd1cf48aa131047772523723a10c230db12fb6e2df`) and `PhoneNumberMetadataForTesting.xml`, as well as the parsing, validation, classification and formatting logic ported to R. |
| [Python `phonenumbers`](https://github.com/daviddrysdale/python-phonenumbers) `v9.0.43` | Apache-2.0 | Independent port of `libphonenumber` at the same metadata version, used as the test oracle across all upstream example numbers, awkward edge cases and 20,000 random and perturbed numbers. |

## What is compiled from `PhoneNumberMetadata.xml`

`data-raw/build-metadata.R` compiles `data-raw/upstream/PhoneNumberMetadata.xml`
(`v9.0.43`) into `R/sysdata.rda` (70 KB compressed):

- **245 CLDR regions** (`"AC"` through `"ZW"`) and **9 non-geographic `"001"`
  calling codes** (`+800`, `+808`, `+870`, `+878`, `+881`, `+882`, `+883`,
  `+888`, `+979`), for **254 territories** in total.
- **Country-code-to-region tables**, with the `mainCountryForCode="true"`
  territory placed first when multiple regions share a calling code (for
  example, `"US"` first among the 25 NANPA territories under `+1`, `"GB"` first
  under `+44`, `"RU"` first under `+7`, `"AU"` first under `+61`, `"IT"` first
  under `+39`).
- **Possible lengths** (`national` and `localOnly`) per number type and their
  territory-wide union on `generalDesc` (with `localOnly` lengths that are
  valid `national` lengths under another type in the same territory removed from
  `generalDesc`'s local-only set, matching `BuildMetadataFromXml.java`).
- **Anchored regular expressions** (`^(?:...)$`) for `generalDesc` and the ten
  number types (`fixedLine`, `mobile`, `tollFree`, `premiumRate`, `sharedCost`,
  `personalNumber`, `voip`, `pager`, `uan`, `voicemail`), plus
  `noInternationalDialling`.
- **Prefix and formatting rules**: `internationalPrefix`,
  `nationalPrefix`, `nationalPrefixForParsing`, `nationalPrefixTransformRule`
  (such as Argentina's `0... 15-...` to `9...` mobile transform),
  `preferredExtnPrefix`, and all `<availableFormats>` `<numberFormat>` rules
  (both national and `<intlFormat>` overrides, with `$NP` and `$FG` resolved
  against the first group referenced in the format template).

## How correctness is checked

1. **Every upstream `<exampleNumber>` (5,705 test cases).**
   `PhoneNumberMetadata.xml` (`v9.0.43`) ships 1,141 `<exampleNumber>` entries
   across all 254 territories and number types. Each example number is tested in
   five input forms — raw national string with its territory's `region`, E.164,
   `INTERNATIONAL`, `NATIONAL` and `RFC3966` — and checked against Python
   `phonenumbers` `9.0.43` on `country_code`, `national_number`, `possible`,
   `valid`, `type`, `region` and all four output formats (`E164`,
   `INTERNATIONAL`, `NATIONAL`, `RFC3966`). Disagreements: **0**.
2. **Hand-written awkward cases (69 cases).**
   Shared calling codes (`+1` across US/CA/BS/BB/JM/PR/VI/GU and unassigned
   NANPA prefixes; `+44` across GB/GG/IM/JE where sub-regions without top-level
   `leadingDigits` require full pattern matching; `+7` RU/KZ; `+61` AU/CX/CC;
   `+262` RE/YT; `+358` FI/AX; `+212` MA/EH; `+599` CW/BQ; `+39` IT/VA), all
   nine `"001"` non-geographic calling codes, significant leading zeros in
   Italy (`+39 06 6981`), Argentina's `011 15-...` mobile transform vs
   `011 ...` fixed line, redundant `(0)` trunk prefixes inside international
   numbers (`+41 (0) 44 668 18 00`), IDD prefixes (`00`, `011`, and `+00`
   retry), extensions (`ext.`, `x`, `#`, `;ext=`, `,,`, and second-number
   `/x2303` stripping), RFC 3966 `tel:` URIs with `;phone-context=` and
   `;isub=`, alpha vanity numbers (`+1-800-FLOWERS`), fullwidth Japanese and
   Arabic-Indic digits, and 7-digit US local-only numbers. Disagreements with
   Python `phonenumbers` `9.0.43`: **0**.
3. **20,000 random and perturbed numbers.**
   Generated with fixed seed `20261114` across six families:
   - 4,000 single-digit substitutions of valid example numbers;
   - 3,000 truncated and extended example numbers;
   - 3,000 prefix perturbations (`++`, fullwidth `＋`, `00`, `011`, bare
     calling codes, trunk `0`, `+00`);
   - 3,000 extension, `Tel:` prefix, `/x999` second-number and RFC 3966
     `;phone-context=` / `;isub=` variations;
   - 3,000 vanity alpha strings, fullwidth digits, Arabic-Indic digits and
     random punctuation separators;
   - 4,000 random digit strings of lengths 1 to 22 with and without `+`.
   Checked against Python `phonenumbers` `9.0.43` across all outputs (`parse`,
   `possible`, `valid`, `type`, `region` and all four `format` modes).
   Disagreements: **0 / 20,000**.
4. **Malformed and hostile input.**
   Empty strings, whitespace, `NA`, 10,000-character strings, malformed
   `phone-context` parameters, HTML/SQL fragments and emoji return `FALSE` or
   `NA` without raising a condition.
5. **Speed.**
   Distinct strings are deduplicated before regex evaluation and evaluated in
   vectorized ICU regex batches per calling code. On an Apple M4 (R 4.6.0), one
   million phone numbers drawn from 10,000 distinct values take 0.13 seconds
   through `phone_valid()` and 0.21 seconds through `phone_parse()`; the
   20,000 distinct random and perturbed numbers in the fuzz suite take 1.8
   seconds.

## Out of scope

- Whether a number is assigned to a subscriber or currently reachable.
- Finding phone numbers inside running text (`piinata` handles scanning text).
- Sub-national geocoding, carrier-name lookup, or time-zone lookup tables.
- Short-number metadata (`ShortNumberMetadata.xml`) such as emergency codes
  (`911`, `112`).
